parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file passes. AssignTaskUseCase.execute only does application-layer work. It loads the task and the user through injected domain repository interfaces and throws an error if either is missing. It then builds an updated Task entity with the new assignee, saves it through the repository abstraction and returns it. The file has no persistence code (no SQL, ORM or file I/O), no transport or HTTP handling and no framework code. Its only business-like logic is two existence checks, which are normal use-case preconditions rather than domain invariants. One small design smell: the use case copies every Task field to set the assignee instead of calling a domain method such as task.assignTo(userId), which suggests an anemic domain model. That is still orchestration, though, not a responsibility that belongs to another layer kind, so it does not fail the rubric.
